subject: Islamic Studies
board: TGA Islamic Studies scheme (aqeedah, fiqh, seerah, hadith, akhlaq)
source: Adapted from TGA Drive RE/Islamic Studies folder (Al-Baseerah Salah quiz KS2: blessings, gratitude, praying on time, the nafs delaying prayer, best deeds); National Curriculum RE (KS2) | Spring 1 2027 (lessons 1, 4, 5 upgraded, 13 and 14 new): Year 3 pack Islamic Studies Spring 1 weeks 1 to 5 (tawheed bridge; arrival in Madinah; first masjid; brotherhood; call to prayer); Bukhari reports on the Hijrah, the masjid land, the brotherhood and the adhan described, not quoted; school seerah text for children TO CONFIRM

lessons.title: Tawheed bridge: Allah is One, the Creator
lessons.bigQuestion: Could a beautiful house build itself? What does that tell us about the world?
objectives: To understand that tawheed means Allah is One and that everything we see is a sign of Him
successCriteria: Most: give three signs of Allah in creation
Some: explain why we worship only Allah
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: awe and wonder at creation

keywords.def: believing Allah is One, with no partner
Allah, who made everything from nothing
a sign of Allah; also a verse of the Qur'an
everything we do to please Allah

hook.text: Could a beautiful house build itself? What does that tell us about the world?
hook.a: Everything made needs a maker. The world shows us Allah, the Creator.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent' (al-Ikhlas 112:1-4).

starter.q: How many pillars of Islam are there?
How many pillars of iman are there?
Name the first pillar of iman.
Which surah tells us Allah is One?

teach.heading: What is tawheed?
bullets: He has no partner, no parent, no child
teach.note: Recite Surah al-Ikhlas (112:1-4) together and explain each ayah simply. Tawheed is the most important thing a Muslim believes.

teach.heading: Signs everywhere
teach.note: Ask pupils to add their own signs in the chat.

teach.heading: Only Allah
teach.note: Link: if Allah alone made us, then He alone deserves our worship (Allah created us to worship Him, 51:56).

misconception.wrong: We can ask a lucky charm to keep us safe
misconception.right: Only Allah protects; we ask Him in du'a

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

options: Allah is One with no partner
check.why: Tawheed means Allah is One. Surah al-Ikhlas says nothing is like Him.

practice.a: Tawheed means Allah is One and we worship only Him.
practice.model: Tawheed means Allah is One. He has no partner. So I worship only Him.

practice.q: Name two signs of Allah in the sky.
practice.a: For example: the sun, the stars

practice.q: Who do we ask when we need help?

independent.q: Make a 'signs of Allah' poster: draw and label four signs from nature.
independent.a: Four labelled signs, for example sun, rain, tree, bird.
independent.model: Teacher draws rain falling on a plant and writes: Allah sends rain so plants grow.

independent.q: Extend: write the meaning of Surah al-Ikhlas in your own words.
independent.a: Allah is One; He needs nothing; He has no parent or child; nothing is like Him.

independent.q: Stretch: why is it wrong to worship anything other than Allah?
independent.a: Because only Allah created us and gives us everything.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: what does a well-built world tell us?
exit.a: It has a Maker: Allah, the Creator.

lessons.homework: Find three signs of Allah at home or outside and tell your family how each one shows Allah's power.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards for the signs. EAL: key words with pictures. Stretch: add a sign from the human body and explain it.
resources: School-approved seerah text for children (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: signs of Allah poster

pictures.alt: A house being built: a house needs a builder

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Tawheed: believing in Allah alone
lessons.title: The Shahadah: La ilaha illa Allah
objectives: Say and explain both parts of the shahadah
Explain what it means to worship Allah alone
Explain that Muhammad ﷺ is Allah's final messenger

keywords.def: one sent by Allah to deliver His message

starter: What is the purpose of life?
What did Jibril teach in the hadith?

teach.heading: The first pillar
bullets: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. The shahadah is the entrance to Islam and the first pillar (hadith of Ibn Umar, Bukhari and Muslim). Echo the Arabic. Ask: what does each word mean? Build the meaning step by step.

teach.heading: No god but Allah
bullets: La ilaha: no one deserves worship
Allah is the only true God
teach.note: Explain that 'ilah' is the one worshipped; the shahadah denies all false gods and affirms Allah alone. Ask: what are false things people worship today? Money, fame, idols. Keep it simple and respectful.

teach.heading: Muhammad is Allah's messenger
teach.note: The second half means we believe he is Allah's servant and messenger. He is the last prophet (33:40: seal of the prophets). Obeying him is obeying Allah (4:80). Misconception: loving the Prophet ﷺ is not worshipping him; we worship Allah only.

teach.heading: Living the shahadah
teach.note: Ask: how would someone live by the shahadah? Collect examples. Link to prophets' call to tawheed (Nuh, Ibrahim).

teach.heading: Words and actions
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever dies knowing that there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise (Muslim, Uthman). Qur'an 47:19 says: know that there is no god but Allah. Stress knowledge, sincerity and living by it, not just saying the words.

practice: Say the first part of the shahadah.
independent: Write the shahadah in English and explain each half
Create a poster: 'Living the shahadah' with four actions
Answer: why is La ilaha illa Allah the key to Islam?
exit: Why do we believe in the Prophet ﷺ?
lessons.homework: Write the shahadah and meaning on a card for a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: word-by-word meaning grid. Stretch: link the shahadah to the story of Ibrahim.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Tawheed: believing in Allah alone
lessons.title: Shirk: associating partners with Allah
objectives: Define shirk and explain why it is serious
Give simple examples of shirk
Explain that Allah forgives those who repent

keywords.def: worshipping or asking anyone besides Allah
calling on Allah and asking Him

starter: What does La ilaha illa Allah mean?

teach.heading: The greatest wrong
bullets: Luqman told his son: do not commit shirk
teach.note: Bismillah. Read 31:13. Explain shirk is giving to someone else what only belongs to Allah. Recall Ibrahim and the idols. Keep a calm, loving tone: tawheed is mercy.

teach.heading: What is shirk?
teach.note: Give examples: idols, praying to saints or the dead, asking creation for what only Allah can give. Clarify it is fine to ask a living person for help they can give (like a teacher) but not to ask anyone but Allah for what only Allah can do.

teach.heading: Dua is for Allah
bullets: 'When you ask, ask Allah' (Tirmidhi, Ibn Abbas)
teach.note: Tell the hadith: if you ask, ask Allah; if you seek help, seek Allah's help (Tirmidhi). Also Qur'an 2:186: I am near and I answer. Link to dua habits.

teach.heading: The way back
teach.note: Allah says He does not forgive that partners be set up with Him, but forgives what is less than that for whom He wills (4:48), and Allah invites those who transgressed not to despair of His mercy (39:53). Say both gently. Do not scare children.

teach.heading: Examples activity
bullets: Is it help? Yes or no
teach.note: Show short scenarios: asking a parent for lunch (fine), praying to a statue (shirk). Discuss with sensitivity; avoid accusing any community.

independent: Sort scenarios: tawheed / shirk / ordinary help
Write a paragraph explaining shirk using 31:13
Make a 'ways to avoid shirk' list
exit: Who do we call on in dua?
lessons.homework: Learn the dua 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah...' (2:201) and explain it to someone.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with symbols; sentence frames. Stretch: explain the difference between asking Allah and asking people.

lessons.title: Arriving in Madinah: the welcome of the Ansar
lessons.bigQuestion: Imagine a family moves into your street with nothing. How could you make them feel welcome?
objectives: To understand how the people of Madinah welcomed the Prophet ﷺ after the Hijrah
successCriteria: All: order the journey from Makkah to Quba to Madinah
Most: say who the Ansar were
Some: explain how the Ansar showed kindness

keywords.def: the city the Prophet ﷺ moved to
the journey from Makkah to Madinah
the Muslims of Madinah: the helpers
a village near Madinah where he stopped first

hook.text: Imagine a family moves into your street with nothing. How could you make them feel welcome?
hook.a: Greet them, share food, help them settle. The Ansar did all this.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us' (at-Tawbah 9:40), the words the Prophet ﷺ said to Abu Bakr in the cave.

starter.q: What does tawheed mean?
starter.a: Allah is One with no partner
options: Allah is One with no partner

starter.q: Where was the Prophet ﷺ born?
Who hid in the cave with the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah?
Name one sign of Allah.

teach.heading: Why did he leave Makkah?
teach.note: Recap the Hijrah briefly. Abu Bakr was with him; Allah says 'Do not grieve, indeed Allah is with us' (at-Tawbah 9:40).

teach.heading: The journey
teach.note: Point at the map. Explain Quba is just outside Madinah.

teach.heading: The Ansar welcome him
bullets: People came out to greet him
Everyone wanted him as a guest
He stayed with Abu Ayyub al-Ansari
teach.note: The people of Madinah waited every day outside the city. His camel knelt near the home of Abu Ayyub, who became his host.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

options: The Muslims of Madinah who helped
The people who hurt the Muslims
check.why: Ansar means helpers: the Muslims of Madinah.

practice.q: Put in order: Madinah, Makkah, Quba, cave.
practice.model: First he left Makkah. Next he hid in the cave. Then he stopped at Quba. Last he reached Madinah.

practice.q: Who was the Prophet's ﷺ host in Madinah?

independent.q: Write a diary entry from a child in Madinah on the day he arrived. Use 'First', 'Then', 'I felt'.
independent.a: For example: First we waited at the edge of the city. Then we saw him coming. I felt so happy.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first line: 'First, we waited outside the city in the hot sun.'

independent.q: Extend: give two ways the Ansar were kind.
independent.a: They welcomed him and offered their homes.

independent.q: Stretch: why did he build a masjid at Quba first?
independent.a: Worship of Allah came first in the new home.

exit.q: The first stop near Madinah was ...
Back to our ponder: one way to welcome a new family, like the Ansar did.
exit.a: For example: share food and offer help.

lessons.homework: Tell your family the journey of the Hijrah in four steps using the words first, next, then, last.
lessons.send: SEND: four picture cards to order. EAL: sentence starters 'First ... Then ...'. Stretch: diary includes a feeling and a reason.
resources: School-approved seerah text for children (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Map of Makkah and Madinah (shown on screen)
Pupil PDF worksheet: Madinah diary frame

pictures.alt: A map showing Makkah and Madinah

lessons.title: Brotherhood: the Muhajirun and the Ansar
lessons.bigQuestion: Would you share half of everything you own with someone you met yesterday?
objectives: To understand how the Prophet ﷺ joined the Muhajirun and the Ansar as brothers
successCriteria: All: say who the Muhajirun and Ansar were
Most: retell the story of Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf and Sa'd
Some: explain what brotherhood means today
lessons.smsc: Social: generosity and care for newcomers

keywords.def: caring for each other like family

hook.text: Would you share half of everything you own with someone you met yesterday?
hook.a: The Ansar offered just that. Brotherhood in Islam makes people family.

islamicLink.text: Allah says the Ansar 'give them preference over themselves, even though they are in need' (al-Hashr 59:9).

starter.q: What were the walls of the first masjid made of?
Who sold the land for the masjid?
What does Ansar mean?
Name one use of the masjid.

teach.heading: Two groups, one family
teach.note: Explain that the Muhajirun had left homes and money behind.

teach.heading: Paired as brothers
bullets: Each Muhajir paired with an Ansari
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ joined them as brothers. Allah praises the Ansar who preferred others over themselves (al-Hashr 59:9).

teach.heading: Sa'd and Abdur-Rahman
bullets: He asked: show me the market
teach.note: Bukhari reports this. Abdur-Rahman made du'a for Sa'd's family and wealth, then worked hard as a trader. Generous giver; hard-working receiver.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: What did Abdur-Rahman ask Sa'd for?
check.why: He chose to work and earn, while thanking Sa'd for his kindness.

practice.a: Muslims who moved from Makkah to Madinah
practice.model: The Muhajirun were Muslims who left Makkah. They moved to Madinah for the sake of Allah. They left their homes behind.

practice.q: What two good things did Abdur-Rahman show?

independent.q: Write a short speech-bubble conversation between Sa'd and Abdur-Rahman (four lines).
independent.a: Sa'd offers to share; Abdur-Rahman thanks him, makes du'a and asks for the market.
independent.model: Teacher writes line 1. Sa'd: 'My brother, take half of what I have.'

independent.q: Extend: how can you be like the Ansar to a new pupil?
independent.a: For example: show them around and include them.

independent.q: Stretch: why was it good that Abdur-Rahman chose to work?
independent.a: He did not want to be a burden; he earned his own living.

exit.q: The Prophet ﷺ joined the Muhajirun and Ansar as ...
Back to our ponder: what did the Ansar's sharing show?
exit.a: That Islam makes Muslims one family who care for each other.

lessons.homework: Do one act of brotherhood or sisterhood this week (share, help, include) and write one sentence about it.
lessons.send: SEND: two-column picture sort. EAL: speech-bubble frame. Stretch: link to 59:9 and explain 'preferred others over themselves'.
resources: School-approved seerah text for children (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Map of Makkah and Madinah (shown on screen)

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Seerah: the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah
lessons.title: The Battle of Badr: trust in Allah
objectives: Explain why Badr took place
State who fought and when
Explain what the Qur'an says about Badr

keywords.def: the first major battle in Islam
relying on Allah while taking steps

teach.heading: Why Badr?
bullets: The Quraysh had harmed the Muslims
teach.note: Bismillah. Keep factual. The Muslims had been driven out and their property taken. Badr took place in Ramadan 2 AH. Avoid glorifying violence; focus on defence, trust and justice. Show a map of Badr.

teach.heading: Numbers
teach.note: Say 'about' since sources give approximate figures. The Muslims set out to intercept a caravan but met the army. The Prophet ﷺ consulted his Companions. Link to shura.

teach.heading: The dua
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ made long dua
teach.note: In Muslim (Umar), he faced the Qiblah and made dua until his cloak fell; Abu Bakr put it back. Qur'an 8:9: when you sought help from your Lord, He answered you that He would reinforce you with a thousand angels. Keep the numbers as in the Qur'an.

teach.heading: Victory
teach.note: Qur'an 3:123: Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak. Ask: what makes people strong? Faith, preparation, trust.

teach.heading: Mercy
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ advised good treatment
teach.note: Reported in Seerah: prisoners were given food and some could free themselves by teaching Muslim children to read. Treat as 'reported'. Link to justice and mercy.

practice: Name the Muhajirun and the Ansar.
What did the Prophet ﷺ do in difficult times?
independent: Write a news report on Badr with 5 facts
Explain tawakkul using Badr as an example
Draw a map of Makkah, Badr and Madinah
exit: What did the Prophet ﷺ do before the battle?
lessons.homework: Find the meaning of tawakkul and use it in a sentence about school.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: fact cards and word bank. Stretch: compare reliance on Allah with laziness.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: purity and the call to prayer
lessons.title: Salah: times and rak'ahs
objectives: Give the number of rak'ahs of each fard prayer
Match prayer times to the sun
Explain why salah is important
starter: Name two things that break wudu.

teach.heading: Gift of salah
bullets: Salah was given on the night of Isra and Mi'raj
The reward is as of fifty
teach.note: Bismillah. Bukhari and Muslim: the prayers were first fifty, then reduced to five, but the reward remains fifty. Explain 'Isra and Mi'raj' briefly; Year 5 will cover it. Show gratitude.

teach.heading: Number of rak'ahs
teach.note: Write on a table. Fard rak'ahs in the day: 17 in total. The Qur'an says prayer is prescribed at fixed times (4:103). Use a prayer clock.

teach.heading: Prayer times
bullets: Dhuhr: after the sun passes midday
teach.note: Maghrib: after sunset; Isha: after the red twilight disappears. Times change by season; use a local timetable. Show a reliable local prayer timetable. Avoid giving exact minutes.

teach.heading: On time
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ loved prayer on time
Ibn Mas'ud asked: which deed is most loved?
He said: prayer at its time
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim. The next deeds: kindness to parents, then striving in Allah's way. Link to the Al-Baseerah Salah lesson where this was highlighted.

teach.heading: Excuses
bullets: Ask a friend to remind you
teach.note: The Al-Baseerah Salah talk pointed out the nafs tries to delay prayer. Discuss strategies: reminders, praying with family. Praise honest ideas.

practice: Name the five prayers in order.
independent: Complete the table: prayer / time / rak'ahs
Make a personal prayer timetable for one day
Write a paragraph on why we pray on time
lessons.homework: Make a prayer timetable for your family this week and note which prayers you prayed on time.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: table with pictures. Stretch: calculate the total fard rak'ahs and explain.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: purity and the call to prayer
lessons.title: The adhan and iqamah
objectives: Say the words of the adhan
Explain how the adhan began
Know what to say in response

keywords.def: the second call before prayer starts
the one who calls the adhan

teach.heading: How the adhan began
bullets: Muslims wanted a way to call people
Abdullah ibn Zayd had a dream
The Prophet ﷺ told Bilal to call it
teach.note: Bismillah. Reported by Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi. The Prophet ﷺ said the dream was true and told Bilal to give the call because he had a beautiful voice. Keep wording: it was a true dream shown to the Companion.

teach.heading: The words
bullets: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah
teach.note: Say the first lines and the call 'come to prayer, come to success'. In the Fajr adhan add 'As-salatu khayrun minan-nawm'. Echo and teach meaning.

teach.heading: Responding
bullets: Say 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' after hayya alas-salah
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said when you hear the mu'adhdhin say what he says (Bukhari and Muslim). The addition after the hayya lines is in Bukhari and Muslim. Dua after adhan: allahumma rabba hadhihid-da'watit-tammah... (Bukhari). Teach as a class if time.

teach.heading: Iqamah
bullets: Called just before the prayer begins
teach.note: Explain iqamah. Straighten lines: the Prophet ﷺ said straighten rows because straight rows are part of perfecting prayer (Bukhari and Muslim). Demonstrate lines on screen.

teach.heading: Role play
teach.note: Pairs practise the first four lines. Praise confident voices. Be mindful of children who are shy.

independent: Write the first five lines of the adhan with meanings
Role-play response with a partner
Explain why the call is important
exit: What do we say when we hear the adhan?
lessons.homework: Listen to the adhan this week and respond as you learned.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: adhan text in transliteration with meaning. Stretch: explain the extra line in Fajr.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: purity and the call to prayer
lessons.title: Purity: wudu in depth
objectives: Explain why wudu is needed
State the obligatory parts of wudu
List what nullifies wudu

keywords.def: extra actions the Prophet ﷺ did

starter: What do we say after wudu?
What is the importance of wudu?
Name two things that break wudu.

teach.heading: Command in the Qur'an
bullets: Allah tells us to wash the face
Wipe head and wash feet to ankles
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 5:6. Read the verse in English: when you rise for prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows, wipe your heads, and wash your feet to the ankles. Explain these are the obligatory acts.

teach.heading: Sunnah acts
bullets: Rinse mouth and nose, use siwak
teach.note: Mention Sunnah acts from authentic reports, e.g., rinsing the mouth and nose (Bukhari and Muslim, Uthman's wudu). Using siwak is encouraged (Bukhari and Muslim). Do not list contested acts. Different madhhabs have different details; follow your school's guidance.

teach.heading: What breaks wudu?
bullets: Anything from the front or back passage
teach.note: Explain these simply. Different scholars hold different views on other matters, such as touching; refer children to their parents' school of thought. Keep the lesson on the agreed points.

teach.heading: Is my prayer valid?
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah does not accept prayer without purification
teach.note: Muslim (Ibn Umar). Ask: if I made wudu, then slept deeply, can I pray? No, repeat wudu. Practise with scenarios.

teach.heading: Quick quiz
teach.note: Give 5 scenario cards. Children vote with thumbs. Discuss.

practice: Where is wudu mentioned in the Qur'an?
What do we say at the start?
independent: Write the obligatory parts of wudu in order
Complete scenario cards: needs wudu or not
Create a wudu reminder poster
exit: Name two things that break wudu.
lessons.homework: Teach wudu to a younger sibling or family member and record how it went.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: step pictures; use scenario cards. Stretch: research the meaning of 'siwak'.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Hadith and akhlaq: intention, gratitude and character
lessons.title: Actions are by intentions
objectives: State the hadith about intentions
Explain why intention matters
Apply the hadith to daily life

keywords.def: what Allah gives for good deeds

teach.heading: The hadith
teach.note: Bismillah. The Prophet ﷺ said: actions are only by intentions and each person will have what he intended. Say it slowly. Ask: what does this mean?

teach.heading: Same action, different intention
bullets: Giving to help vs to show off
Studying for knowledge vs to impress
Praying for Allah vs for people
teach.note: Present pairs of acts. Ask which is rewarded. Explain that intention changes an act from habit to worship.

teach.heading: Turn habits into worship
bullets: Eating to have strength to obey Allah
teach.note: Brainstorm: how can we make a good intention? Say Bismillah and have a purpose. Note: intention is in the heart; no need to say it aloud for ibadah.

teach.heading: Showing off
teach.note: Define riya. Avoid frightening; focus on correcting the heart. Allah knows our intention. Link to the Al-Baseerah talk: the soul tells us to delay; sincere intention helps.

teach.heading: Setting intentions
teach.note: Children write one intention for the week. Share with a partner.

independent: Rewrite four activities to include a good intention
Explain the hadith in your own words (5 sentences)
Make a 'Niyyah bookmark' with a reminder
exit: Give one example of a good intention.
lessons.homework: Choose one daily activity and set an intention before doing it; reflect after.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with images. Stretch: explain the difference between habit and worship.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Hadith and akhlaq: intention, gratitude and character
lessons.title: Shukr and sabr: gratitude and patience
objectives: Define shukr and sabr
Explain the hadith of the believer's affair
Give examples of both
starter: What is the purpose of life?

teach.heading: Count your blessings
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 16:18. Ask children to list as many blessings as possible in one minute. Use the Al-Baseerah Salah quiz: why can't we count Allah's blessings? Ask what the arrogant person forgets.

teach.heading: Gratitude grows blessings
bullets: 14:7: if you are grateful I will increase you
Thank Allah with tongue, heart and actions
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said the one who does not thank people does not thank Allah (Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi). Show ways to thank: words, deeds, dua.

teach.heading: Patience
teach.note: Three types of sabr: on obedience, away from sin, and on hardship. Ask for examples. Link to earlier lessons: Nuh, Bilal.

teach.heading: The believer's affair
bullets: Everything is good for the believer
If good comes, he is grateful
If harm comes, he is patient
teach.note: Muslim (Suhayb). Read slowly. Ask: how does this give peace? Emphasise both are from faith.

teach.heading: Practise
bullets: Say Alhamdulillah for what you have
teach.note: Pairs role-play: you lose a game; you win. What would a grateful, patient person do? Praise responses.

independent: Write three things you are grateful for and who to thank
Write a short paragraph on a time you were patient
Create a shukr and sabr poster
lessons.homework: Keep a gratitude journal for three days.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: word bank for feelings. Stretch: explain how both good and hard times bring reward.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Hadith and akhlaq: intention, gratitude and character
lessons.title: Good character and controlling anger
objectives: Explain that good character is highly valued
Explain the hadith of the strong man
Practise strategies to control anger

teach.heading: Best character
bullets: The best of you are those with the best character
The Prophet ﷺ had the best character
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 68:4: and indeed you are of a great moral character. Ask: what does good character look like? Gather examples.

teach.heading: The strong man
bullets: The strong one is not the wrestler
teach.note: Read the hadith. Ask: why is self-control a strength? Give anger scenarios (unfair game, sibling takes something).

teach.heading: What to do when angry
teach.note: A'udhu billah is in Bukhari and Muslim (Sulayman ibn Surad). The Prophet ﷺ advised sitting if standing (Abu Dawud, hasan). Practise slow breathing and staying quiet or speaking gently.

teach.heading: After anger
teach.note: Qur'an 3:134: those who restrain their anger and pardon people; Allah loves the doers of good. Role-play apologies.

teach.heading: My character plan
teach.note: Pairs share. Teacher notes common goals. Praise honesty.

practice: Name a trait of good character.
independent: Write a plan for controlling anger with three steps
Role-play a calm response to a scenario
Explain the strong man hadith in your own words
exit: What should we say if we feel angry?
What does the hadith say about strength?
lessons.homework: Practise one anger strategy this week and report back.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: feelings cards and sentence frames. Stretch: explain why forgiveness is strong.

lessons.title: Building the first masjid in Madinah
lessons.bigQuestion: If you moved to a new town, what is the first building you would want to find, and why?
objectives: To understand why the Prophet ﷺ built the masjid first and how everyone helped
successCriteria: All: say what the masjid was built from
Most: explain why the masjid came first
Some: describe what the masjid was used for
lessons.smsc: Social: working together for the community

keywords.def: the Prophet's ﷺ masjid in Madinah
to make something by putting parts together

hook.text: If you moved to a new town, what is the first building you would want to find, and why?
hook.a: A masjid: it is the heart of a Muslim community.

islamicLink.text: Allah praises a masjid 'founded on righteousness from the first day' (at-Tawbah 9:108).

starter.q: What does Ansar mean?
Where did the Prophet ﷺ stop before Madinah?
Who was his host in Madinah?
What does Hijrah mean?
starter.a: The journey from Makkah to Madinah

teach.heading: The land
bullets: Land belonged to two orphan boys
The Prophet ﷺ paid for it
He did not just take it
teach.note: Bukhari reports the land was bought from two orphan boys. Ask: what does this teach us? (Be fair, pay for what you take.)

teach.heading: Everyone helped
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ carried bricks too
teach.note: Bukhari describes the walls of mud brick, pillars of palm trunk and a roof of palm branches. Leaders help with the work.

teach.heading: More than a prayer hall
teach.note: Ask pupils which are still true of masajid today.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ do while the masjid was built?
check.why: He worked beside the Companions: a leader who helps.

practice.q: What was the masjid made from?
practice.a: Mud bricks, palm trunks and palm leaves
practice.model: Walls: mud bricks. Pillars: palm trunks. Roof: palm leaves. Simple, but full of iman.

practice.q: Why did he pay for the land?
practice.a: To be fair to the orphan boys
options: To be fair to the orphan boys

practice.q: Name one use of the masjid apart from prayer.

independent.q: Label a drawing of the first masjid: walls, pillars, roof, and what each was made of.
independent.a: Walls: mud brick; pillars: palm trunks; roof: palm leaves
independent.model: Teacher draws one wall and labels it 'mud brick wall'.

independent.q: Extend: write two sentences on how everyone helped.
independent.a: Everyone carried bricks. The Prophet ﷺ carried bricks too.

independent.q: Stretch: why do you think the masjid came first?
independent.a: Prayer and worship of Allah are the centre of Muslim life.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: why is the masjid the heart of a community?
exit.a: We pray, learn and help each other there.

lessons.homework: Ask an adult about your local masjid: what happens there besides prayer? Bring one fact.
lessons.send: SEND: picture labels to drag onto the drawing. EAL: word bank (brick, palm, roof). Stretch: compare the first masjid with a masjid today.
resources: School-approved seerah text for children (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: label the first masjid

pictures.alt: A palm trunk like the first pillars

lessons.title: The community learns to call to prayer
lessons.bigQuestion: Before clocks and phones, how could a whole town know it was time to pray together?
objectives: To understand how the Muslims of Madinah came to use the adhan to call people to prayer
successCriteria: All: say why the community needed a call to prayer
Most: retell how the adhan was chosen
Some: say the first words of the adhan and what they mean
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: answering the call to prayer

keywords.def: the person who calls the adhan
people who live, pray and work together

hook.text: Before clocks and phones, how could a whole town know it was time to pray together?
hook.a: The Muslims thought about bells, horns and fires, then chose the human voice: the adhan.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O you who have believed, when [the adhan] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah' (al-Jumu'ah 62:9).

starter.q: Who were the Muhajirun?
What did Abdur-Rahman ask Sa'd for?
What were the masjid pillars made of?
How many daily prayers are there?

teach.heading: A problem to solve
bullets: People came to the masjid at different times
They met to decide what to do
teach.note: Bukhari reports the Muslims of Madinah gathered and discussed how to call people to prayer.

teach.heading: Ideas they talked about
teach.note: Explain that Muslims wanted their own way, not copying others' worship.

cards: A man calling with his voice

teach.heading: Bilal calls the adhan
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ told Bilal to call
teach.note: Bukhari reports the Prophet ﷺ said to Bilal to stand and call for prayer. Other reports describe a Companion, Abdullah ibn Zayd, seeing the words in a dream. Say the opening words: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ (Allahu akbar: Allah is the Greatest).

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Who was the first person to call the adhan?
check.why: Bilal was told by the Prophet ﷺ to call; he became the first mu'adhdhin.

practice.q: Why did the Muslims need a call to prayer?
practice.a: So everyone knew when to come and pray together
practice.model: People arrived at different times. They wanted to pray together. So they needed a signal that everyone could hear.

practice.q: The person who calls the adhan is the ...

independent.q: Draw a four-box story strip: the problem, the meeting, the choice, Bilal's call. Add a caption to each.
independent.a: Problem: people did not know the time. Meeting: ideas shared. Choice: a voice. Bilal called the adhan.
independent.model: Teacher captions box 1: 'People came to pray at different times.'

independent.q: Extend: what should we do when we hear the adhan?
independent.a: Stop, listen, repeat the words and get ready to pray.

independent.q: Stretch: why is a human voice a good way to call to prayer?
independent.a: It uses Allah's words of praise and calls people kindly.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: how did Madinah know it was time to pray?
exit.a: Bilal called the adhan with his voice.

lessons.homework: Listen to the adhan at home (from the masjid or a prayer-time app) and repeat the words after the mu'adhdhin.
lessons.send: SEND: four picture boxes with sentence strips. EAL: adhan opening words with meaning card. Stretch: explain why Muslims chose their own way.
